message.content:
Several prominent figures challenged Copernicus's heliocentric model during his lifetime and after his death. The Roman Catholic Church, particularly under Pope Paul IV in 1542, condemned the Copernican system as contrary to Scripture. Tycho Brahe, a respected astronomer, rejected the full Copernican model in favor of his own geo-heliocentric compromise. John Calvin, the Reformed theologian, expressed strong theological objections to the idea that Earth was not the center of creation.

Why would a model that placed the Sun at the center of the universe be so threatening to the intellectual establishment of the 16th century? Who could argue against the apparent evidence of the Sun and stars moving across the sky each day? How could theologians accept that humanity occupied a mere planet in an orbital dance around the Sun? Was it not more reasonable, to the critics, to preserve the geocentric framework that had governed thought for over a millennium?

What a radical departure from Aristotelian physics Copernicus dared to propose! How bold was it to overturn centuries of Ptolemaic authority in a single book! What fierce opposition met the *De revolutionibus* when it was first published in 1543! How daring was the young Polish canon to challenge the very foundations of natural philosophy!
